name: Sumitomo Electric Industries
whyWatching:
Sumitomo Electric is a Japanese company that makes wires, cables, optical fiber, batteries and the attachments that go with them — and it’s one of the core suppliers for Meta’s brand-new **Petal** subsea cable, announced September 21, 2026. Petal is the first *petabit-class* transoceanic cable — France to the U.S., roughly **7,000 km**, twice the capacity of today’s best cables — and Sumitomo is providing the **two-core fiber** at the heart of it, with NEC building the system.

This is exactly the kind of pick I like: an unglamorous industrial that quietly makes the thing everyone’s about to need, *before* the whole world catches on. The dividend is kind of lame and inconsistent — but that’s not why I’m here. This is a bet on the cable, and on being early.
catalyst: Meta’s **Petal** cable — announced Sep 21, 2026, in service targeted for 2029. First petabit-class transoceanic system; France–US, ~7,000 km, ~2× the capacity of today’s best cables. Sumitomo supplies the two-core fiber. (Meta’s bigger 50,000 km “Waterworth” project is separate.)
positionNote: I put $50 in — small, deliberate, and disclosed in the open.
